meta.what: Northern land squares that the pipeline's bare-ground screen leaves out and that still hold some bare ground: long-spell low-Sun hours on snow-free ground in the winter half and the whole year.

screen_relaxed.kept_here: 0 < bare share < min_bare and bare_km2 >= the floor

meta.floor_meaning: counts_by_region and the terrain pass use the main floor; leads lists every square at or above the smallest floor shown, with at_main_floor true or false
meta.snow_odds_rule: as in grazing_cells.json: measured squares use the odds as mapped, doubtful squares the odds with the stale-flag rule; counts are over measured squares, doubtful ones apart

rim.what: Shetland, Orkney and the Faroe Islands in the land-cover file (squares with at least 20 percent land): how many squares, and how much bare ground the screen hides there

horizon.chosen: the 300 squares at the main floor with the most winter hours on snow-free ground for any target, and every square of Shetland, Orkney, Faroe Islands at any floor shown

computed: long-spell hours over a flat horizon, winter half and whole year, 16 targets, every square at or above the smallest floor
the same on snow-free ground (ten-day snow-free odds of the 4 km snow maps) with snow status and pixels
the same after terrain for the squares of meta.horizon
share of the winter snow-free hours with the Sun within 90 degrees of south
counts by region at 50 and 100 winter hours, and the same counts for the screened squares
not_computed: what the bare ground is (beach, tidal flat, rock, quarry)
squares with less than 20 percent land
slope and the other scores of cells_scored.json
warnings: Snow-free odds at a coast rest on few land pixels of the 4 km snow maps: see snow.land_pixels of snow.block_pixels for each lead. Squares with snow status 'doubtful' use the lower odds of the stale-flag rule and are counted apart.
No cloud is taken into account. The Atlantic rim is very cloudy in winter; these are hours of Sun geometry on ground that is probably free of snow, not hours of visible Sun.
WorldCover's bare class at a coast can be beach, tidal flat, rock, a quarry or other worked ground. What the bare ground of a lead is was not looked at.

The land-cover file is a sample: one 10 m pixel about every 900 m (12 samples per 0.1 degree). South of 64.5 N one bare sample stands for about 0.4 km2, so the 0.25 km2 floor means one bare sample, 1 km2 means three or more and 3 km2 seven or more; bare_km2 of a lead with few samples (bare_samples) is uncertain by about its own size, and a square with bare ground between the samples reads as having none.
Squares with less than 20 percent land were left out when the land-cover file was built, so small islands and skerries are not here at all.
The terrain horizon was computed only for the squares named in meta.horizon; winter_hours_after_terrain is null elsewhere and the counts after terrain cover only squares that have a horizon.

Hours after terrain are an average over all the land of a square (the share of its land that sees the Sun), not over its bare ground. A bare summit or headland can see more of a low southern Sun than that average, a quarry or beach under a hill less.
The winter half runs from 28 September to 31 March. North of about 67 N the hours counted here fall in October and March, not in midwinter.
Region names come from rough latitude and longitude boxes (first match wins); a square near a border can carry its neighbour's name.
Hours are for a 365-day year with standard refraction, a 2 h minimum spell and 1-minute steps, as in the pipeline; the limits listed in section (i) of RESULTS.md apply here too.

fields.winter_hours_flat: long-spell hours, 28 September to 31 March, flat horizon, no snow
fields.winter_hours_snow_free: the same times the snow-free odds of each ten-day period
fields.winter_hours_after_terrain: the same counted only where the terrain horizon of the square leaves the Sun in view (share of the square's land); null where no horizon was computed
fields.bare_samples: bare samples of the land-cover reading behind bare_km2, if every sample was mapped
fields.south_share_winter: share of winter_hours_snow_free with the Sun within 90 degrees of south
fields.best_ten_day_periods: the three ten-day periods of the winter half with the most snow-free hours
